symptoms: DKA: HGT >= 11 mmol/l, younger age, onset hours-days, nausea/vomiting, abdominal pain, acidotic Kussmaul breathing, urine ketones positive, metabolic acidosis, anion gap > 16
HHS: HGT >= 30 mmol/l, elderly, onset several days, altered mental state, focal neuro signs, urine ketones negative/weak, osmolality > 350, normal anion gap (12-16)

management_steps.details: If shocked: Balsol/Ringers Lactate 20ml/kg bolus. DKA: 1st litre over 1 hour, 2nd litre over 1 hour, then maintenance to UO 1-2ml/kg/hr. HHS: 250-500 ml/hr. Change to 5% Dextrose water when HGT <= 15 mmol/l or serum Na > 150 mmol/l.
Potassium: Add 20-40mmol/l to IV fluids to maintain K at 4-5 mmol/l. Magnesium: 2g MgSO4 in fluids. Sodium Bicarbonate 8.5%: 1 ml/kg IV over 30 min ONLY if pH <= 6.85, tCO3 < 5.
Delay insulin until serum K+ > 3.5 mmol/l. Actrapid 0.1 u/kg IV STAT (max 10u) then hourly OR Actrapid infusion @ 0.1 u/kg/hr. HHS anticoagulation: Clexane 0.5 mg/kg SC STAT.

warnings: Delay insulin until serum Potassium > 3.5 mmol/l to prevent lethal hypokalaemic cardiac arrest.
